title: I made 20 AI analyst personas debate every US stock instead of giving one AI "pick" (dev here)
author: seviniryusuf
selftext:
I'm the developer, so take this as a builder sharing, not an ad.

Most AI stock tools give you one confident answer. I went the other way: a panel of 20 AI analyst personas (value, growth, momentum, risk and so on) each scores a stock and they often disagree. You see the bull case, the bear case and why, and the blend becomes a 0–100 score split into technical, fundamental and sentiment.

You can test your own read with paper trading ($100k virtual cash, live prices), so it's a sandbox rather than a signal service. No buy/sell calls, no return claims.

Short tour of the live app: https://gettickr.ai/tour?c=reddit_ai_trading

Curious what people here think: does a disagreeing panel actually help you reason about a trade, or is one well-explained model better?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: 20 personas off the same model share the same training and the same blind spots, so a lot of that disagreement is just wording.

replies.author: seviniryusuf
replies.body:
Fair hit, and mostly right. The written theses all come from one model with different persona prompts, so yes, a lot of that "disagreement" is framing, not independent judgment.

The number underneath isn't an LLM though: the 0-100 score is deterministic (technicals, fundamentals vs sector medians, sentiment), and the personas only change how those are weighted and explained. I oversold "20 analysts debating" in the title. The honest version is one scoring engine with a few lenses on it.

Mixing models from different providers per persona would be the real fix for shared blind spots. Has that worked for you anywhere?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair, and then the deterministic score is what deserves the testing. bucket every name by score each week and check whether the 80+ group beats the under-20 group over the next month. if it does, the personas are just the packaging on top, and that's fine.
